roles.entrypoint: By path: the module src/main.ts or src/main.tsx, and nothing else, so the checks tell one entrypoint and no second program's. Its helpers are the functions it leaves unexported; a module of wiring that entrypoints share has no directory, and is reported as having no role.
roles.driving-adapter: By path: every module under src/adapters/driving/. The checks don't tell a driving adapter's entry from the helpers that serve its contract, or one driving adapter from another. The checks tell no helper from a member: every module there counts as a member, and a helper is a function or type a module leaves unexported.
roles.driven-adapter: By path: every module under src/adapters/driven/, whether or not anything in it implements a port. The checks tell no helper from a member: every module there counts as a member, and a helper is a function or type a module leaves unexported.
roles.port: Not told. A port is an interface declared in its orchestrator's module, under src/orchestrators/, and the checks hold it to what they hold orchestrator code to: nothing tells an interface that is a port from any other declaration there.
roles.orchestrator: By path: every module under src/orchestrators/, the ports declared there included. The checks tell no helper from a member: every module there counts as a member, and a helper is a function or type a module leaves unexported.
roles.decision: By path: every module under src/core/. The checks don't tell a decision from a value: the one core directory holds both, and each is held to what the core is held to.
roles.value: By path: every module under src/core/. The checks don't tell a value from a decision: the one core directory holds both, and each is held to what the core is held to.
roles.fake: By path: every module under src/fakes/, whether or not anything in it has a port's shape. One declared in a test file (*.test.ts) is test code to the checks, with no role. The checks tell no helper from a member: every module there counts as a member, and a helper is a function or type a module leaves unexported.

role-paths.summary: The ESLint and dependency-cruiser configs give each module under src/ one role by its path, and verify checks that a file in each role's directory has that role's rules.

unplaced-modules.summary: no-restricted-syntax reports every module under src/ but tests that is in none of the roles' directories, nor in src/fakes/ or src/testing/, which has no role.

depcruise-core-is-pure.summary: core-is-pure: a module under src/core/ imports none of the project's own code outside src/core/. Packages and host modules are left to imports-reach-nothing-impure.

depcruise-orchestrators-import-no-adapte.summary: orchestrators-import-no-adapter: no orchestrator imports a module under src/adapters/.

depcruise-orchestrators-are-pure.summary: orchestrators-are-pure: no orchestrator imports a Node built-in.

depcruise-driving-adapters.summary: driving-adapters-import-no-driven-adapter: no module under src/adapters/driving/ imports one under src/adapters/driven/.

depcruise-driven-adapters.summary: driven-adapters-import-only-core-and-driven-adapters: a module under src/adapters/driven/ imports only the core and other driven adapters.

depcruise-entrypoint-is-not-imported.summary: entrypoint-is-not-imported: no module but a test imports src/main.ts.

depcruise-only-tests-import-fakes-and-te.summary: only-tests-import-fakes-and-test-code: no module but a test imports one under src/fakes/ or src/testing/, the test code a project ships for the tests of projects that depend on it, apart from the modules of those two directories. test-code-imports-no-adapter keeps a module under src/testing/ from importing an adapter.

depcruise-fakes.summary: fakes-import-only-core-orchestrators-and-fakes: a module under src/fakes/ imports nothing else under src/ but the core, the orchestrators, where the ports are declared, and other fakes.

depcruise-no-container.summary: no-container: no module imports a dependency-injection container: inversify, tsyringe, typedi, awilix and others.

depcruise-no-circular.summary: no-circular: no module depends on itself through others.

no-effects.summary: ESLint rule ts-ianf-strict-baseline/no-effects, in the core and the orchestrators: no global that performs an effect (timers, crypto, fetch, storage, process, console, globalThis), no new Date() or Date.now(), no Math.random(), and no module-level let or var.

imports-reach-nothing-impure.summary: ESLint rule ts-ianf-strict-baseline/imports-reach-nothing-impure, in the core: it resolves each import of a package or host module as Node does, with the import conditions, and reads every module that import loads, at any depth, CommonJS and ES modules alike, with typescript-eslint's parser and scope analysis. It reports a host module; an import it can't resolve, and a require or import() of a computed name; a global other than ECMAScript's own pure ones, eval, Function, Date, Intl, process and console among those reported; Math.random; localeCompare and the toLocale methods; a change to a built-in; a module-scope binding that a function assigns, writes through or changes with a mutating method; and a module-scope regular expression with the g or y flag whose lastIndex a function can see. Each report names the path from the core's import to the operation and the line it is on. Its verdicts are kept for the run, by package name, version and install location.

no-configuration.summary: ESLint rule ts-ianf-strict-baseline/no-configuration, everywhere but src/main.ts and tests: no process.env, process.argv, import.meta.env or parseArgs.

max-lines-edges.summary: max-lines-per-function limits functions in src/adapters/ and src/main.ts to 50 lines.

complexity.summary: complexity is at most 10 everywhere: a warning, which check's --max-warnings 0 makes fail.

union-types.summary: A TypeScript union is closed: no other module can add a member, and the type checker rejects a value outside it.

no-implicit-any.summary: tsc with strict, which verify requires: a parameter or field with no type, and nothing to infer one from, is an error rather than an any.

banned-syntax.summary: no-restricted-syntax bans enums, default and optional parameters, optional properties of object types and interfaces, let and var, and a class extending anything but JavaScript's own errors.

switch-exhaustiveness.summary: @typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check: a switch on a union names every member, and has no default arm once it does, with considerDefaultExhaustiveForUnions and allowDefaultCaseForExhaustiveSwitch off.

no-param-reassign.summary: no-param-reassign: no function assigns to one of its parameters, including from a closure.

prefer-readonly.summary: @typescript-eslint/prefer-readonly: a private field that is never reassigned is declared readonly.

no-unused-result.summary: ESLint rule ts-ianf-strict-baseline/no-unused-result: no expression statement drops a Result.

no-unused-vars.summary: @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars: no variable is assigned and never read.

no-empty.summary: no-empty: no block is empty, unless it holds a comment.

no-explicit-any.summary: @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: no type is written as any.

no-unsafe-any.summary: @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment, no-unsafe-argument, no-unsafe-call, no-unsafe-member-access and no-unsafe-return: a value of type any isn't assigned to a typed variable, passed, called, read from or returned.

no-unsafe-function-type.summary: @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-function-type: no type is written as Function.

no-non-null-assertion.summary: @typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion: no value is asserted defined with the ! operator.

no-implied-eval.summary: @typescript-eslint/no-implied-eval: no function is built from text with new Function, and no text is passed as code to setTimeout, setInterval or setImmediate.

dot-notation.summary: @typescript-eslint/dot-notation: a field named by a string literal is read with a dot, where the type checker enforces private.

ban-ts-comment.summary: @typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment: no @ts-ignore or @ts-nocheck comment, and no @ts-expect-error comment without a description.

test-mocks.summary: no-restricted-properties, in tests: no vi.mock or vi.spyOn.

prettier-check.summary: The shared check task runs prettier --check, and verify requires a project's check to run the shared one.

verify-prettier.summary: verify reports a Prettier option that differs from @ianflanagan1/ts-ianf-strict-baseline/prettier.

verify-settings.summary: verify reads the project's settings as each tool resolves them, and reports a tsconfig strictness option of the baseline's that isn't on, one of the ESLint rules it lists that isn't an error, in general or in its role's files, a banned syntax the project dropped, and a dependency-cruiser rule of the baseline's that isn't an error.

verify-shared-tasks.summary: verify requires a project's check, format and lint-file tasks to run the baseline's own, which run every check, ts-ianf-strict-baseline verify among them, over the whole project, and counts none run with ignore_error.

shared-task-caches.summary: The shared tasks keep Prettier's, tsc's and ESLint's caches under cache/, and verify requires a project's check, format and lint-file tasks to run the shared ones.

verify-gitignore.summary: verify reports a .gitignore without the line /cache/, or a project without one.

core-calls-reach-nothing-impure.gap: State kept through this, as an object's method that changes its own field does, or through a local that holds a module-scope value, isn't seen, and nor is a change made by passing a module-scope value to a function other than Object.assign, Object.defineProperty and their kind, or by a method other than the mutating ones of arrays, maps and sets. Math.random reached by destructuring or a computed member passes. A method called replace, match, split or search is taken by its name for String's, so a global regular expression given to another object's method of that name passes. Totality isn't checked: a function that throws passes. ESLint's cache keeps a core module's result until that module or the config changes, so an upgraded package is read again only then, or with the cache cleared. It reads what a module's code does, not which of its functions the core calls: one operation anywhere in a module the import loads is reported, even where nothing the core calls reaches it. Whatever it can't follow is reported rather than passed: a require or import() of a computed name, an import it can't resolve (a native addon, a tsconfig path alias or a package.json imports entry among them), code it can't parse, a feature test such as typeof window, and a callback a module runs while it loads that writes a module-scope value, which it takes for a function run later.

Math.random reached by destructuring or a computed member passes. A method called replace, match, split or search is taken by its name for String's, so a global regular expression given to another object's method of that name passes. Totality isn't checked: a function that throws passes. ESLint's cache keeps a core module's result until that module or the config changes, so an upgraded package is read again only then, or with the cache cleared.
